catalog_quote: 2.3. Stress placement. The position of primary stress in a word is determined. Prefixes and infixes do not occur with stress. Roots always occur stressed when suffixes are not present. Retained stress roots occur stressed when inherently stressed suffixes are not present; variably stressed roots yield stress to suffixes. Inherently stressed suffixes always occur stressed; inherently unstressed suffixes never occur with stress. Variably stressed suffixes receive stress from variably stressed roots. 2.31. Retained stress roots. xʷúl 'turn' xʷúleke 'drill'; ník 'cut' sníkəmə? 'sawdust'. 2.32. Variably stressed roots. xʷík 'cut fish' ... túkʷ 'cover' stukʷcín 'mute'. 2.33. Inherently stressed suffixes. sources.citation: Idsardi, William James. 1991. Stress and glottalized sonorants in Shuswap. Papers for the 26th International Conference on Salish and Neighbouring Languages (ICSNL 26), Vancouver: UBC, pp. 217-232.
sources.quote: 'Stress in Salish is largely determined morphologically. Descriptively, roots are divided into strong and weak types, and suffixes into strong, variable and weak (vowelless). Stress placement is often described as a hierarchy with the highest member in the word receiving the stress: (4) STRESS HIERARCHY strong suffix > strong root > variable suffix > weak root [> weak (vowelless) suffix]', quoting Kuipers 1974 §13.2 ('Verbs ... fall into two types depending on whether they are I base-stressed or II suffix-stressed') and §13.8; table (13): Shuswap root+strong suffixes -> last suffix stressed, w

sources.citation: Kamigaki-Baron, Michelle. 2021. Acoustic description of Secwepemctsín vowels. Papers for ICSNL 56 (UBCWPL), pp. 134-153.
sources.quote: Instrumental F1/F2 study of stressed vs unstressed vowels (two Western-dialect speakers, 2020-21) testing Kuipers (1989) claim that unstressed vowels reduce to schwa; finds only unstressed /e/ partially reduces. Stress position is taken from the Kuipers orthography; no statement on stress placement.

sources.citation: Hendricks, Sean. 1998. Shuswap diminutive reduplication. In Maye & Miyashita (eds.), Proceedings of SWOT IV, U. Arizona (ERIC ED454710), pp. 5-12.
sources.quote: Diminutive reduplicant is infixed after the stressed vowel and copies the pre-stress consonant (data from Kuipers 1974); passing remark 'Stress is predictable in Shuswap, and therefore, not marked in the input.' No placement rule given.

sources.note: A 7-page commentary on the phonemic transcription of Kuipers 1974 (The Shuswap Language) - vowel vs resonant interpretation, schwa, automatic vs inherent rounding, biuniqueness; no tone, pitch, accent or intonation term anywhere in the text; word stress is presupposed as given (stressed vs unstressed syllables decide [u i] = /u i/ or /w y/, pp.2-3; 'with a redundant stress mark', p.4; '/i/ and /u/ occur in stressed syllables only', p.6) but not analysed; no tone system stated or implied (no-tone by implication only, not an explicit denial); n_tones not applicable.
